waiting on the same missing mechanic is a build order.

## combat-only-permanent-shield

Blocks **15** cards.

- **(op)** a `combat_only: true` option on the `prevent_damage_permanent` op (a field on structs.PermanentShield read by primitives.damage_permanent / damage_player), so a resolving ability can install a this-turn shield that stops only COMBAT damage dealt to and dealt by one targeted permanent
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `prevent_damage_permanent` with dealt: to_and_by and duration: this_turn is the right shape but stops ALL damage, so noncombat burn at the creature and its own ping/fight damage would also be prevented (a strictly better card); `combat_only` exists only on the `prevent_damage` static, which is continuous on a printed permanent and cannot be installed on a target for a turn by an activated ability
- **(op)** a `combat_only: true` option on the `prevent_damage_permanent` op (and its PermanentShield), so a resolving ability can prevent only COMBAT damage dealt to and/or by a permanent for this turn, leaving burn, fight and other noncombat damage untouched
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `prevent_damage_permanent` takes `dealt: to_and_by` and `duration: this_turn` but has no combat-only filter, so it would also stop noncombat damage (a strictly different card); the `prevent_damage` static has `combat_only` but is continuous while its source stands (no 'this turn', cannot be installed by an activated ability) and only stops damage dealt TO what it matches, never damage the creature deals; the one-shot `grant_ability` op cannot grant a static
- **(op)** a `combat_only: true` option on the `prevent_damage_permanent` op (a field on the permanent shield read by the damage primitives), so a resolving activated ability can install a this-turn shield that stops only COMBAT damage dealt to and dealt by one targeted permanent

The may-pay {G}{G} and return_to_hand halves are expressible once the event exists.

## activate-only-as-an-instant

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** a timing restriction on an activated mana ability that bars it from being activated during the casting or cost-payment of a spell (rule 605.3a / the Lion's Eye Diamond ruling) while leaving it activatable whenever the player has priority: a flag legality and the mana solver both read, so costs.solver_taps and the payment planner never reach for it and only a priority activation can
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: 'sorcery_speed_only' is the opposite restriction -- it narrows activation to the main phase with an empty stack, where this line needs the *wider* instant timing minus the mid-cast window mana abilities uniquely get. 'activation_condition' is documented as a board question ('Activate only if you control five or more Vampires'), checked by legality against the game state, and cannot ask what the player is in the middle of doing. Nothing else in cost_keys or the ability fields describes when an ability may be activated. Dropping the sentence is not neutral: a plain is_mana_ability would be picked up by the solver while paying for another spell, so the engine would discard the player's hand on its own to help pay for a spell -- the precise thing the printed restriction forbids. The near-miss of setting is_mana_ability false hides it from the solver but pays a different price: the mana would then be produced on resolution from the stack, so the ability could be countered or responded to and could not be used to pay for a spell already being cast, which is the only reason anyone plays this card.

Nothing in `static_effects` reaches the stack at all: `ward` and `protection` are the closest, and both tax or forbid *targeting* a permanent while leaving countering untouched, and `spell_cost_reduction` is the only static that looks at spells and it only changes their price. ## conditional-mana-ability

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** a mana ability whose production is switched by a condition on its source at activation time -- "Add {C}; if this has a luck counter on it, instead add one mana of any color". `mana_options_of` and the payment solver must be able to evaluate a per-branch condition against live game state (here `counters_on` for a luck counter on the source) and offer only the branch that is currently true, in both the automatic tap path and the manual-mana path
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_split_mana_rider` (src/commanderblitz/cards/loader/mana.py) allows only leading `add_mana`/`choose_mode` effects plus a rider drawn from MANA_RIDER_OPS = {add_counters, add_poison, damage, gain_life, lose_life, remove_counters}; `if` is not in that set, so the printed conditional is a load error, not a card. `_mana_options` freezes production into a fixed tuple of 6-tuples at load time and `_mana_amount` may only scale one `add_mana`'s symbols, so no state can change *which* symbol is produced -- only how many. The three state-dependent forms that do exist (`mana_reflects`, `mana_identity`, `mana_chosen_color`) are each hardcoded questions about the board, the command zone or the permanent's chosen colour, and each is required to be the ability's only effect; none can be a condition on counters and none can pick between two branches. `choose_mode` is not a substitute and would be an approximation, because a mode is a free choice at activation: the land would offer any colour with no luck counter on it. Splitting the line into two mana abilities gated by `activation_condition` is silently wrong rather than merely ugly: `costs._sources_of` (src/commanderblitz/engine/costs.py) collects solver mana sources on `solver_taps` plus tapped/summoning-sickness/abilities_locked alone and never consults `activation_condition`, so the payment solver would happily tap the counter-less Caverns for any colour; `activation_condition` is only read on the offered-action path in `legality` (src/commanderblitz/engine/legality.py). It would also leave one printed line claimed by two abilities, which the residual gate reads as text nobody owns.

- **(value)** flip_coin recording its results under an `as` binding (the way roll_dice does for `rolled`), with a value reading how many of the flips made by this effect were won/lost, so "if you won five flips this way" can be an `if` on that count
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: flip_coin takes only `effects`/`else` per single flip and records nothing; inside a `repeat` the win branch can draw and the loss branch can deal damage, but no value counts the wins afterwards. set_turn_flag on a loss is only a near miss: it persists across a second attack the same turn and so would misread a later all-wins resolution

</details>

## free-cast-by-other-player

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a caster key on the free-cast ops (exile_until's cast_free, and play_exiled) naming a player spec other than the effect's controller, so "its controller exiles cards from the top of their library until they exile a nonland card, then THEY may cast that card without paying its mana cost" offers the cast to the destroyed permanent's controller (e.g. {"controller_of": <snapshot binding>}) and that player controls the resulting spell
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: exile_until already walks another player's library via `player`, but its docstring and code route the free-cast offer to ctx.controller always (_offer_free_cast(ctx, controller, ...)), which is Strago and Relm's "You may cast that card"; play_exiled, cast_card and cast_from_hand likewise cast as the resolving controller. Writing it that way would hand the opponent's free spell to the Flourish's caster, a strictly different (and much stronger) card. Demonstrate itself and the conditional destroy (destroy `as` + an `if` on `exists`) are expressible; only the caster of the free spell is not.

## impulse-from-opponent-library

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a way to exile the top N cards of a *named* player's library and leave the impulse permission on the ability's controller rather than on that library's owner. Either a new key on look_at_top -- a 'playable_by' (or 'playable_controller') that makes _move_found write obj.playable_by = ctx.controller instead of the pid it looped over -- or, more generally, an 'as' binding on look_at_top recording the cards it moved (the way mill and exile already record theirs), so a following grant_playable can name them. Ragavan needs exactly one of these; with the binding, 'exile the top card of that player's library' becomes look_at_top {player: {binding: 'event_player'}, amount: 1, destination: 'exile', as: 'pilfered'} and 'until end of turn, you may cast that card' becomes grant_playable over {binding: 'pilfered'}
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: look_at_top is the only op that reaches the top of a library, and its playable_this_turn branch in effects/ops_cards.py _move_found hardcodes obj.playable_by = pid -- the player whose library was looked at. On Ragavan that library is the *opponent's*, so the printed 'you may cast that card' would grant the permission to the very player whose card was stolen: the opposite of the card. The exile op does set playable_by = ctx.controller, which is the right seat, but it takes a selector and selector_keys has no way to name the top of a library (no 'top'/'from_top' key; zone: 'library' with a count resolves to a chosen card from the whole deck, which is a tutor, not the top card). Composing the two also fails: look_at_top calls move_object without a 'by', so nothing records exiled_by and a follow-up grant_playable over {zone: 'exile', exiled_with: 'self'} matches nothing, while {zone: 'exile', player: ...} would match every card that player has ever had exiled. look_at_top has no 'as' binding either -- mill has one (Locke, Treasure Hunter) and exile has one, so this op is the odd one out. Naming 'that player' is NOT the gap: {"binding": "event_player"} already resolves to the damaged player, since primitives.damage_player fires COMBAT_DAMAGE_TO_PLAYER with player=pid.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer** (rank 271) — `ragavan_nimble_pilferer`
  - Whenever Ragavan deals combat damage to a player, create a Treasure token and exile the top card of that player's library. Until end of turn, you may cast that card.

</details>

- **(selector)** the `modified` key (true: has a counter, is equipped, or is enchanted by an Aura its controller controls) accepted in a trigger `filter`, so a `deals_combat_damage_to_player` trigger with filter {controller: you, types: [Creature], modified: true} fires only for a creature that is modified when it deals the damage
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `modified` is in selector_keys and static_affects_filter_keys (so the trample line is expressible), but not in trigger_filter_keys / engine.triggers.TRIGGER_FILTER_KEYS, which the loader enforces. An any_of of has_counters and enchanted_by in the trigger filter misses the equipped limb (`equipped` is not a trigger filter key either; `attached` means attached to the ability's source). Moving the test into the trigger's `condition` as an `exists` over the subject binding makes it an intervening-if that is rechecked on resolution, so a creature that loses its counter or Equipment before resolution would wrongly find no land -- a different card.

</details>

## no-mana-cost

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** A card that prints no mana cost (Ancestral Vision, Lotus Bloom, Living End, Restore Balance, Wheel of Fate) must not be castable for its mana cost: its mana cost is unpayable (118.6, 202.1b), so it may be cast only by an alternative or free cast such as suspend's cast_for_free. The engine needs a distinction between 'no mana cost' and '{0}', and legality must withhold the ordinary hand cast line for the former while still offering the suspend special action and free casts.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The `suspend` card-level key ({"cost": "{U}", "counters": 4}), a player target and `draw` with `player: {"target": "t1"}` express every printed word, but an omitted `mana_cost` compiles to an empty ManaCost, which legality treats as {0}. Verified with a scratch run of verify(): the draft passed all six gates because the sandbox CAST it straight from hand for nothing, so the card would be a free 'target player draws three cards' at sorcery speed -- strictly better than printed. No card-level rider (`cant_cast_first_turns`, `alternative_cost`, a `cant_cast_spells` static) says 'this card cannot be cast from hand normally' while leaving the suspend free cast open.

</details>

## noted-mana-type

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** an effect that records which mana type was actually spent to pay the activation cost of the ability being resolved, and stores that type on the source permanent as a persistent note that survives until it is overwritten by a later activation
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The closest value is `colors_of_mana_spent`, which returns the *number* of distinct colors spent to cast the object at `source_oid` (sunburst/converge) -- it is a count, not a type, it is read off a cast spell rather than an activation payment, and nothing writes it onto a permanent as durable state. `set_flag` records only a named boolean, and `add_counters` records only a count of a fixed counter kind, so neither can hold a mana type.
- **(value)** a mana specification for `add_mana` that resolves to the mana type previously noted on the source permanent, so the second ability produces exactly that type
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `add_mana` takes a literal mana string parsed by `parse_mana_production`, and `add_mana_per` only scales a literal unit by a selector count; neither can read state off the source. A mana ability may contain only `add_mana` or one `choose_mode` of `add_mana` modes, so the only expressible shape is a free choice among the five colors -- that is a strictly better card than the printed one, which is locked to the type banked earlier, so it is an approximation, not a translation. `choose_color` is likewise a fresh choice at resolution and is not legal inside a mana ability.

## spells-cast-per-player

Blocks **1** card.

- **(value)** a value leaf that reports spells cast this turn *per player* rather than summed -- e.g. a `max_spells_cast_of: "each_opponent"`, or a per-player quantifier over a condition -- so "if **an opponent** cast three or more spells this turn" asks whether any single opponent reached three. Wanted by the whole Trap cycle and by storm-watching cards (Mindbreak Trap, Archmage Ascension-style counters, Guttersnipe-adjacent per-seat thresholds).
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `alternative_cost` with `{"mana": "{0}"}` and a `condition` is exactly the right home for this line -- that half is not the blocker. The condition itself is: `spells_cast_this_turn` (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/values.py) resolves its player spec through `select_players` and then **sums** the ledger across every seat it names, so `{"spells_cast_this_turn": "each_opponent"}` is the *total* spells cast by all opponents. At a pod that is a strictly wider card than the printing: three opponents casting one spell each would switch on the free cast, which Mindbreak Trap does not do. The per-player machinery that exists, `max_count_of`/`min_count_of` via `_counts_per_player` (values.py), counts *objects* matching a selector one seat at a time and has no reach into the turn ledger's `spells_cast`; `condition_keys`' `any`/`all` combine sibling conditions and do not quantify over players.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Mindbreak Trap** (rank 539) — `mindbreak_trap`
  - If an opponent cast three or more spells this turn, you may pay {0} rather than pay this spell's mana cost.
  - Exile any number of target spells.

</details>

## stack-wipe

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a non-targeted mass stack op (or a selector the counter/exile ops can read with zone 'stack') that, on resolution, exiles every other spell on the stack (moving the card to exile without countering it, so 'can't be countered' spells are exiled too and copies cease to exist) and counters every activated and triggered ability on the stack
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: op_counter resolves only declared targets ('target') or one value-named 'sid'; it ignores 'objects', so there is no 'all spells/abilities' form, and countering would also be wrong for the spell half since uncounterable spells must still be exiled. op_exile chooses objects through choose_objects over zone-held cards and has no path that removes a StackItem from the stack. The 'object_kind'/'ability_kind' selector keys only narrow an ability_on_stack target

</details>

## target-if-cast-during
